Level 2 layout:
- Top board: white 4-row × 7-column cell grid (rows 9-24, columns 7-46), 4 green dots on row 2 (rows 15-18): columns 13-16, 19-22, 31-34, 43-46.
- Bottom board: 2×2 cells (rows 45-54, columns 43-52), 1 green dot at rows 51-54, columns 43-46.
- Orange hub: O is at rows 33-36, columns 31-34, surrounded by Y (rows 32-37, columns 30-35).
- Black path (b node): node 4 (rows 8-15, column 49) — a vertical line on the right side of the top board; node 35 (rows 18-27, columns 6-49) — a line below the top board, extending right; node 44 (rows 32-33, column 37); node 46 (rows 36-39, columns 30-37); node 48 (rows 44-57, columns 42-55) — the border of the bottom board.
So the path is: right edge of top board (column 49, rows 8-15) → down → row ~24-27 (node 35 spans rows 18-27, columns 6-49) → right to column 49 → down → to the hub (nodes 44/46 around the hub) → down → bottom board (rows 44-57).
The path connects the right side of the top board, the hub, and the bottom board.
The goal is probably: consolidate all 5 dots into 1 (same as level 1). But now the dots are on separate boards. The path allows dots to move between boards — probably a dot can slide along the path through the hub to another board.
How does the merge mechanic work here? In level 1, select a dot → a ring appears at the position just past the nearest dot in that direction along the track; click the ring → the dot slides and absorbs.
On the top board: 4 dots on the same row (row 2 of the grid): columns 13, 19, 31, 43. Select the leftmost (13-16) → ring just past the next dot (19-22) = columns 25-28? In level 1, the ring was at the position of the empty cell just past the nearest dot. Here the cells are: columns 7, 13, 19, 25, 31, 37, 43 (7 columns). Dots at 13, 19, 31, 43.
Select the dot at 13 → nearest is 19 → ring at 25. Click → dot moves to 25, absorbs 19.
Select the dot at 25 → nearest is 31 → ring at 37. Click → dot at 37.
Select the dot at 37 → nearest is 43 → ring at 49?? But 49 is outside the board (the board ends at column 46; the path is at column 49). Hmm, or the ring is off the board → invalid.
Alternative: select the dot at 43 → nearest is 37 → ring at 31 (just past 37, on the left side). Click → 43 absorbs 37 and lands at 31. Then select the dot at 31 → nearest is 25 → ring at 19. Click → 31 absorbs 25 and lands at 19. 1 dot at 19 on the top board.
Then we need to bring in the dot on the bottom board. How? The path connects the boards. Probably a dot can be moved along the path: select the dot at 19 → the ring appears along the path? The path is on the right side of the board (column 49). Hmm, the dot at 19 is not adjacent to the path.
Maybe: the orange hub is the key. Dots have to be moved to the hub? Or the hub is a "connector" that activates when a dot is placed on it?
Let's think about the path geometry: the path exits from the right side of the top board around rows 8-15 (node 4, column 49, rows 8-15) — that's the right edge of the top board, spanning rows 8-15 (the height of row 1 of the grid?). Then node 35 (rows 18-27, columns 6-49): a long horizontal line below the board, from column 6 to column 49, rows 18-27?? That's a thick band. Hmm, node 35 is a b with 53 pixels, rows 18-27, columns 6-49. That's the lower border of the top board (rows 25-27) plus a right-side extension (rows 18-27, column 49)?
Actually, the top board's border (node 2, B, rows 7-56, columns 5-57) is the big black frame enclosing everything? Node 47 (W, rows 44-55, columns 42-53) is the white of the bottom board.
So the black "path" is actually the border of the connected white regions? No wait — the top board's white (node 3) is rows 8-25, columns 6-47. The bottom board's white (node 47) is rows 44-55, columns 42-53. The black node 2 connects them: it's the outer frame. The white regions are not connected to each other (separated by black).
Hmm, so where is the "path" that the dots travel along? Looking at the image: from the right side of the top board, a black line extends right to column ~57, then down, then left to the hub, then down, then right to the bottom board. The path is drawn as a black line (like the track border in level 1). The track in level 1 was a white region with a black border, and the cells were gray squares.
In level 2, the "track" between the boards is just a black line (no white cells?). The hub (orange) sits on the path.
Maybe the mechanic is: a dot can slide along the track; at the right end of the top board, the track continues through the hub to the bottom board. So the top board + path + bottom board form one continuous track! The cells on the top board are the gray squares; the path segment has no cells, but the hub is a special cell.
So the whole track: top board row 2 (or any row?) → right end → down the path → hub → down → bottom board.
Hmm, but which row of the top board connects to the path? The path connects at rows 8-15 (node 4, column 49, rows 8-15) — that's the right edge of the top board's row 1 (rows 9-12)? Or between row 1 and row 2? Node 4 spans rows 8-15, column 49: the right edge of the top board, from the top border (row 8) to row 15 (the start of row 2). So the path connects to the right side of the top board around rows 8-15 — i.e., the right edge of row 1 (rows 9-12) and the top of row 2.
And node 35 (rows 18-27, columns 6-49): hmm, that includes the bottom border of the top board (rows 25-27, columns 5-47) and a vertical segment at column 49, rows 18-27. Wait, that would mean the path goes: right edge of the top board (column 49) from row 8 to row 27, then… left along row 25-27? No — the bottom border of the top board is at rows 25-27, columns 5-47. Node 35 spans columns 6-49, rows 18-27: that's the bottom border (rows 25-27) + the right column (column 49, rows 18-27)? But the right column of the top board's border is at column 47-48 (node 2?). Hmm, I'm getting confused.
Let me look at the image again: the top board is a 4×7 grid. On its right side, a black line extends right from the top-right area to column ~57, then down to row ~30, then left to the hub (columns 30-35), the hub is at (32-37, 30-35), then from the bottom of the hub a line goes down to row ~44, then right to the bottom board (columns 42-55). The bottom board is a 2×2 grid with 1 dot.
So the path: top board → right → down → left to the hub → down → right to the bottom board. The hub is on the path.
The track is continuous: the top board's cells connect to the path at the top board's right edge (around rows 8-15, i.e., the right side of row 1), and the bottom board connects at its left edge (rows 44-57, columns 42-44 → the left side of the bottom board, rows 45-54).
So the whole thing is one track: [top board 4×7 grid] — right end (row 1) — path — [hub] — path — [bottom board 2×2 grid].

But wait — can a dot even enter the path in the first place? The path has no cells. Maybe the hub is the only "cell" on the path, and dots can only move from the top board to the hub, and from the hub to the bottom board.
Or maybe the mechanic is different: the ring can appear on the path/hub, and the dot slides there.
